maria.chen: Quick question — for the differential routing experiment, how are we planning to credit cache savings back to tenants?
omar.khan: Do we mean at per-request level or amortized per-tenant per-window?
ev an.jones: per-request is ideal but we can't attach precise upstream KV cache hits without huge telemetry overhead.
liam: Agreed. We should avoid high-cardinality metrics per request. idea: attribute credits by route + model variant + time window.
maria.chen: That loses fidelity for bursty tenants though. They might unfairly subsidize others.
omar.khan: true. Another option: sample 1% of requests and extrapolate. cheaper to store and we can estimate variance.
ev an.jones: sampling will bias tiny tenants. we should also have a fallback: if tenant < 1k requests/day, use direct per-tenant accounting.
liam: Can we implement hybrid: sample for large tenants, deterministic prefix-matching for small tenants?
maria.chen: Sounds plausible. How would this show up in Console? what widgets do we need for explainability?
omar.khan: A per-tenant "cache credits" card (daily), plus a breakdown by route/model and a confidence interval from sampling.
ev an.jones: UX note: show estimated vs measured and a link to the sampling rate and sample size. Customers hate silent approximations.
liam: Implementation sketch: telemetry emits sample flag + KV_hit boolean. We aggregate on ingestion to compute hit_rate(route, model, tenant_sampled). Then credits = hit_rate * avg_token_saved * cost_per_token * request_count.
maria.chen: Can you paste the sample event schema?
ev an.jones: ```json
{
  "ts": 1769509999,
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "route": "/chat",
  "model": "gptx-13b",
  "sampled": true,
  "kv_hit": true,
  "tokens_saved": 24
}
```
omar.khan: Nice. We'll need to tag whether the request used local cache vs cross-tenant shared cache. shared cache crediting rules differ.
liam: For shared caches we should prorate credits by tenant token usage on that shard in the same window. Otherwise tenants that never hit still get credits.
maria.chen: What about rollouts? Canary where routing sends traffic to cheaper variant — how do we avoid double-crediting when we fallback?
ev an.jones: Good point. We should mark rollout_id on events and when fallback occurs we attribute the saved tokens to the active variant at request time. If fallback returns to default, no credit for the failed attempt.
omar.khan: Also add a "credit_explanation" link in the console that shows raw sampled events and our extrapolation math for the selected window.
liam: Implementation tasks: 1) telemetry schema change (sampled + rollout_id + cache_shard) 2) ingestion pipeline change to compute hit_rate by (tenant, route, model, shard) with sampling inflation 3) console card + drilldown 4) billing connector to apply credits to usage ledger.
maria.chen: Can we estimate cost to store samples? ballpark numbers?
ev an.jones: If we sample 1% across 10M requests/day -> 100k events/day. at ~1KB/event => ~100MB/day -> ~3GB/month. cheap on our infra.
omar.khan: CPU for aggregations is bigger cost. but we can rollup per-5m windows to cut cardinality.
liam: Proposed SLA for accuracy: for tenants > 100k requests/day maintain +/-5% error; for smaller tenants, fall back to deterministic accounting.
maria.chen: OK please prepare a short RFC with the schema, aggregation math, and Console mock for tomorrow's sync. add a migration plan for retrospective credits.
ev an.jones: I'll draft the RFC and include sample queries for the ingestion job.
omar.khan: I'll mock Console card and the drilldown.
liam: I'll prototype the aggregator with sample data.
sre-bot: deploybot: new branch created: feature/cache-crediting-experiments by evan.jones
maria.chen: thanks everyone. tagging @oncall for visibility — we may need to watch ingestion slots when this lands. :eyes:
thread_summary: Quick thread about designing sampling + attribution for cache savings credits, telemetry schema, console UX, and rollout handling. Decided on hybrid sampling/deterministic scheme, required telemetry fields, aggregation plan, and next steps (RFC + protos).
